			end
			vx = math.clamp(vx :: number, x, x + size)
			vy = math.clamp(vy :: number, y, y + size)
			vz = math.clamp(vz :: number, z, z + size)
		end
		table.insert(verts, Vector3.new(vx, vy, vz))
		cell.vid = #verts
	end

	local function assignVerts(cell: Cell)
		if cell.leaf then
			makeVertex(cell)
		else
			for _, ch in ipairs(cell.children :: { Cell }) do
				assignVerts(ch)
			end
		end
	end
	assignVerts(rootCell)
	local tQef1 = os.clock()

	-- ── Dual Contouring polygon recursion (Ju et al. 2002) ──
	-- Verbatim canonical traversal tables + recursion. A quad is emitted on each
	-- "minimal edge" with a sign change, connecting the 4 surrounding leaves'
	-- vertices. Leaves are reused as they're descended past, so different leaf
	-- sizes stitch crack-free. Tables are 0-based; +1 to index Lua child arrays.
	local tris: { number } = {}

	local cellProcFaceMask = {
		{ 0, 4, 0 }, { 1, 5, 0 }, { 2, 6, 0 }, { 3, 7, 0 }, { 0, 2, 1 }, { 4, 6, 1 },
		{ 1, 3, 1 }, { 5, 7, 1 }, { 0, 1, 2 }, { 2, 3, 2 }, { 4, 5, 2 }, { 6, 7, 2 },
	}
	local cellProcEdgeMask = {
		{ 0, 1, 2, 3, 0 }, { 4, 5, 6, 7, 0 }, { 0, 4, 1, 5, 1 },
		{ 2, 6, 3, 7, 1 }, { 0, 2, 4, 6, 2 }, { 1, 3, 5, 7, 2 },
	}
	local faceProcFaceMask = {
		{ { 4, 0, 0 }, { 5, 1, 0 }, { 6, 2, 0 }, { 7, 3, 0 } },
		{ { 2, 0, 1 }, { 6, 4, 1 }, { 3, 1, 1 }, { 7, 5, 1 } },
		{ { 1, 0, 2 }, { 3, 2, 2 }, { 5, 4, 2 }, { 7, 6, 2 } },
	}
	local faceProcEdgeMask = {
		{ { 1, 4, 0, 5, 1, 1 }, { 1, 6, 2, 7, 3, 1 }, { 0, 4, 6, 0, 2, 2 }, { 0, 5, 7, 1, 3, 2 } },
		{ { 0, 2, 3, 0, 1, 0 }, { 0, 6, 7, 4, 5, 0 }, { 1, 2, 0, 6, 4, 2 }, { 1, 3, 1, 7, 5, 2 } },
		{ { 1, 1, 0, 3, 2, 0 }, { 1, 5, 4, 7, 6, 0 }, { 0, 1, 5, 0, 4, 1 }, { 0, 3, 7, 2, 6, 1 } },
	}
	local edgeProcEdgeMask = {
		{ { 3, 2, 1, 0, 0 }, { 7, 6, 5, 4, 0 } },
		{ { 5, 1, 4, 0, 1 }, { 7, 3, 6, 2, 1 } },
		{ { 6, 4, 2, 0, 2 }, { 7, 5, 3, 1, 2 } },
	}
	local processEdgeMask = { { 3, 2, 1, 0 }, { 7, 5, 6, 4 }, { 11, 10, 9, 8 } }
	local ORDERS = { { 0, 0, 1, 1 }, { 0, 1, 0, 1 } }

	local function processEdge(nodes: { Cell }, dir: number)
		local minSize = math.huge
		local minIndex = 1
		local flip = false
		local scMin = false
		local pem = processEdgeMask[dir + 1]
		for i = 1, 4 do
			local ev = EDGEV[pem[i] + 1]
			local cm = nodes[i].corners
			local m1 = bit32.band(bit32.rshift(cm, ev[1]), 1)
			local m2 = bit32.band(bit32.rshift(cm, ev[2]), 1)
			if nodes[i].size < minSize then
				minSize = nodes[i].size
				minIndex = i
				flip = m1 ~= 0
				scMin = m1 ~= m2
			end
		end
		if not scMin then
			return
		end
		local a, b, c, d = nodes[1].vid, nodes[2].vid, nodes[3].vid, nodes[4].vid
		if not (a and b and c and d) then
			return
		end
		if not flip then
			table.insert(tris, a); table.insert(tris, b); table.insert(tris, d)
			table.insert(tris, a); table.insert(tris, d); table.insert(tris, c)
		else
			table.insert(tris, a); table.insert(tris, d); table.insert(tris, b)
			table.insert(tris, a); table.insert(tris, c); table.insert(tris, d)
		end
	end

	local edgeProc
	edgeProc = function(nodes: { Cell }, dir: number)
		if not (nodes[1] and nodes[2] and nodes[3] and nodes[4]) then
			return
		end
		if nodes[1].leaf and nodes[2].leaf and nodes[3].leaf and nodes[4].leaf then
			processEdge(nodes, dir)
			return
		end
		local mask = edgeProcEdgeMask[dir + 1]
		for i = 1, 2 do
			local m = mask[i]
			local en = table.create(4)
			for j = 1, 4 do
				local nj = nodes[j]
				en[j] = if nj.leaf then nj else (nj.children :: { Cell })[m[j] + 1]
			end
			edgeProc(en, m[5])
		end
	end

	local faceProc
	faceProc = function(a: Cell, b: Cell, dir: number)
		if not (a and b) then
			return
		end
		if a.leaf and b.leaf then
			return
		end
		local sel = { a, b }
		local fm = faceProcFaceMask[dir + 1]
		for i = 1, 4 do
			local m = fm[i]
			local f0 = if a.leaf then a else (a.children :: { Cell })[m[1] + 1]
			local f1 = if b.leaf then b else (b.children :: { Cell })[m[2] + 1]
			faceProc(f0, f1, m[3])
		end
		local fem = faceProcEdgeMask[dir + 1]
		for i = 1, 4 do
			local m = fem[i]
			local order = ORDERS[m[1] + 1]
			local en = table.create(4)
			for j = 1, 4 do
				local nj = sel[order[j] + 1]
				en[j] = if nj.leaf then nj else (nj.children :: { Cell })[m[j + 1] + 1]
			end
			edgeProc(en, m[6])
		end
	end

	local function cellProc(cell: Cell)
		if cell.leaf then
			return
		end
		local ch = cell.children :: { Cell }
		for i = 1, 8 do
			cellProc(ch[i])
		end
		for i = 1, 12 do
			local m = cellProcFaceMask[i]
			faceProc(ch[m[1] + 1], ch[m[2] + 1], m[3])
		end
		for i = 1, 6 do
			local m = cellProcEdgeMask[i]
			edgeProc({ ch[m[1] + 1], ch[m[2] + 1], ch[m[3] + 1], ch[m[4] + 1] }, m[5])
		end
	end

	cellProc(rootCell)
	local tDC1 = os.clock()

	if #verts == 0 or #tris == 0 then
		return nil, "no surface"
	end
	local rawTris = #tris / 3

	-- ── Decimate (QEM) — collapse DC's coplanar/curved cell quads to minimal
	-- geometry while preserving sharp edges. Cheap here: v3's adaptive raw mesh
	-- is already far smaller than a uniform grid's, so QEM has little to chew. ──
	if cfg.decimate ~= false then
		local maxErr = cfg.qemMaxError or (minLeaf * minLeaf * 3)
		local cap = cfg.triCap or 40000
		verts, tris = SdfDecimate.decimateQEM(verts, tris, 1.0, maxErr, 0.0, 14, cap)

		-- Reproject onto the iso-surface. QEM places each collapsed vertex at the
		-- quadric-optimal point — the intersection of its incident planes — which
		-- on a curved surface lies *off* it, re-introducing the chord inset that
		-- barrels/waves curves. One Newton step snaps every vertex back onto
		-- field = 0. Sharp-feature vertices already sit at field ≈ 0 (they're on
		-- the surface), so this barely moves them; the clamp skips any outlier.
		if cfg.reproject ~= false then
			local clamp = maxLeaf
			for i = 1, #verts do
				local v = verts[i]
				local d, gx, gy, gz = SdfField.fieldGrad(root, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)
				d -= soften
				if d > -clamp and d < clamp then
					verts[i] = Vector3.new(v.X - d * gx, v.Y - d * gy, v.Z - d * gz)
				end
			end
		end

		-- Tangential relaxation with flip-prevention. Dual Contouring's vertex
		-- spacing is uneven → smooth surfaces show a "wave" under shading and the
		-- triangulation looks questionable. Slide each smooth vertex along the
		-- surface toward its neighbour centroid (tangent-plane move + reproject)
		-- to even the spacing. Crucially, each proposed move is REJECTED if it
		-- would flip an incident triangle — that's what dented/holed the earlier
		-- attempts (folded geometry). Sharp vertices (incident faces diverge past
		-- sharpRelaxAngle) are pinned so edges/creases survive.
		local relaxIters = cfg.relaxIters or 0
		if relaxIters > 0 and #verts > 0 then
			local nV = #verts
			local nT = #tris // 3
			local adj: { { [number]: boolean } } = table.create(nV)
			local vTris: { { number } } = table.create(nV)
			for i = 1, nV do
				adj[i] = {}
				vTris[i] = {}
			end
			local refN: { Vector3 } = table.create(nV)
			local sharp = table.create(nV, false)
			local cosRelax = math.cos(math.rad(cfg.sharpRelaxAngle or 30))
			local fnx = table.create(nT)
			local fny = table.create(nT)
			local fnz = table.create(nT)
			for t = 1, nT do
				local b = (t - 1) * 3
				local i1, i2, i3 = tris[b + 1], tris[b + 2], tris[b + 3]
				local p1, p2, p3 = verts[i1], verts[i2], verts[i3]
				local fn = (p2 - p1):Cross(p3 - p1)
				local m = fn.Magnitude
				fn = if m > 1e-9 then fn / m else Vector3.yAxis
				fnx[t], fny[t], fnz[t] = fn.X, fn.Y, fn.Z
				local tri = { i1, i2, i3 }
				for _, vi in ipairs(tri) do
					local rn = refN[vi]
					if rn == nil then
						refN[vi] = fn
					elseif fn:Dot(rn) < cosRelax then
						sharp[vi] = true
					end
					table.insert(vTris[vi], t)
				end
				adj[i1][i2] = true; adj[i1][i3] = true
				adj[i2][i1] = true; adj[i2][i3] = true
				adj[i3][i1] = true; adj[i3][i2] = true
			end
			local clamp = maxLeaf
			for _ = 1, relaxIters do
				for i = 1, nV do
					if not sharp[i] then
						local v = verts[i]
						local cx, cy, cz, c = 0, 0, 0, 0
						for nb in pairs(adj[i]) do
							local p = verts[nb]
							cx += p.X; cy += p.Y; cz += p.Z; c += 1
						end
						if c > 0 then
							-- tangent-plane move toward centroid, then reproject
							local _, gx, gy, gz = SdfField.fieldGrad(root, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)
							local dx, dy, dz = cx / c - v.X, cy / c - v.Y, cz / c - v.Z
							local dn = dx * gx + dy * gy + dz * gz
							dx -= dn * gx; dy -= dn * gy; dz -= dn * gz
							local tx, ty, tz = v.X + dx * 0.5, v.Y + dy * 0.5, v.Z + dz * 0.5
							local d, rgx, rgy, rgz = SdfField.fieldGrad(root, tx, ty, tz)
							d -= soften
							local nvx, nvy, nvz
							if d > -clamp and d < clamp then
								nvx, nvy, nvz = tx - d * rgx, ty - d * rgy, tz - d * rgz
							else
								nvx, nvy, nvz = tx, ty, tz
							end
							-- reject if any incident triangle would flip
							local flip = false
							for _, t in ipairs(vTris[i]) do
								local b = (t - 1) * 3
								local a1, a2, a3 = tris[b + 1], tris[b + 2], tris[b + 3]
								local q1 = if a1 == i then Vector3.new(nvx, nvy, nvz) else verts[a1]
								local q2 = if a2 == i then Vector3.new(nvx, nvy, nvz) else verts[a2]
								local q3 = if a3 == i then Vector3.new(nvx, nvy, nvz) else verts[a3]
								local nn = (q2 - q1):Cross(q3 - q1)
								if nn.X * fnx[t] + nn.Y * fny[t] + nn.Z * fnz[t] <= 0 then
									flip = true
									break
								end
							end
							if not flip then
								verts[i] = Vector3.new(nvx, nvy, nvz)
								for _, t in ipairs(vTris[i]) do
									local b = (t - 1) * 3
									local p1, p2, p3 = verts[tris[b + 1]], verts[tris[b + 2]], verts[tris[b + 3]]
									local fn = (p2 - p1):Cross(p3 - p1)
									local m = fn.Magnitude
									if m > 1e-9 then
										fn /= m
										fnx[t], fny[t], fnz[t] = fn.X, fn.Y, fn.Z
									end
								end
							end
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local tDecim1 = os.clock()

	-- ── Adaptive subdivide + project (hero quality) ──
	-- Split an edge only where it's CURVED: take its midpoint, project onto the
	-- iso-surface, and if that moves it off the chord by more than curveTol·len,
	-- keep the projected point (the chord becomes an arc → smooth curves). Flat
	-- faces and crease edges have ~zero deviation → never split → they stay
	-- minimal and sharp (a flat box stays 12 tris). Each face is then re-cut by
	-- how many of its 3 edges split (0/1/2/3 → red-green patterns), so split
	-- edges are shared by both neighbours and there are no T-junction cracks.
	local subdiv = cfg.subdivide or 0
	local curveTol = cfg.subdivideCurveTol or 0.03
	for _ = 1, subdiv do
		local nT = #tris // 3
		local splitMid: { [number]: any } = {} -- edge key → midpoint vid, or false if flat
		local function edgeMid(a: number, b: number): number?
			local lo, hi = a, b
			if lo > hi then lo, hi = hi, lo end
			local key = lo * 33554432 + hi
			local cached = splitMid[key]
			if cached ~= nil then
				return if cached then cached else nil
			end
			local pa, pb = verts[lo], verts[hi]
			local mx, my, mz = (pa.X + pb.X) * 0.5, (pa.Y + pb.Y) * 0.5, (pa.Z + pb.Z) * 0.5
			local d, gx, gy, gz = SdfField.fieldGrad(root, mx, my, mz)
			d -= soften
			local elen = (pb - pa).Magnitude
			local lim = elen * 0.5
			local px, py, pz = mx, my, mz
			if d > -lim and d < lim then
				px, py, pz = mx - d * gx, my - d * gy, mz - d * gz
			end
			local dx, dy, dz = px - mx, py - my, pz - mz
			if math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz) > elen * curveTol then
				table.insert(verts, Vector3.new(px, py, pz))
				local mi = #verts
				splitMid[key] = mi
				return mi
			end
			splitMid[key] = false
			return nil
		end
		local newTris: { number } = {}
		local function emit(a, b, c)
			newTris[#newTris + 1] = a; newTris[#newTris + 1] = b; newTris[#newTris + 1] = c
		end
		for t = 1, nT do
			local b = (t - 1) * 3
			local v1, v2, v3 = tris[b + 1], tris[b + 2], tris[b + 3]
			local m12 = edgeMid(v1, v2)
			local m23 = edgeMid(v2, v3)
			local m31 = edgeMid(v3, v1)
			local cnt = (if m12 then 1 else 0) + (if m23 then 1 else 0) + (if m31 then 1 else 0)
			if cnt == 0 then
				emit(v1, v2, v3)
			elseif cnt == 3 then
				emit(v1, m12, m31); emit(m12, v2, m23); emit(m31, m23, v3); emit(m12, m23, m31)
			elseif cnt == 1 then
				-- rotate so the single split edge is v1→v2
				while not (m12 and not m23 and not m31) do
					v1, v2, v3, m12, m23, m31 = v2, v3, v1, m23, m31, m12
				end
				emit(v1, m12, v3); emit(m12, v2, v3)
			else -- cnt == 2: rotate so the UN-split edge is v3→v1
				while not (m12 and m23 and not m31) do
					v1, v2, v3, m12, m23, m31 = v2, v3, v1, m23, m31, m12
				end
				emit(m12, v2, m23); emit(v1, m12, m23); emit(v1, m23, v3)
			end
		end
		tris = newTris
	end

	-- ── Decimate-after (remesh) ──
	-- QEM on the SUBDIVIDED mesh, then reproject. Subdivision+projection first
	-- built dense geometry that accurately hugs the (softened) surface; QEM now
	-- simplifies THAT, so the minimal vertices land optimally on the smooth
	-- surface instead of being limited by the coarse base. Soft edges survive in
	-- shading via the analytic normals even as the fillet geometry coarsens.
	if cfg.decimateAfter and subdiv > 0 then
		local maxErr = cfg.qemMaxErrorAfter or cfg.qemMaxError or (minLeaf * minLeaf * 3)
		local cap = cfg.triCap or 40000
		verts, tris = SdfDecimate.decimateQEM(verts, tris, 1.0, maxErr, 0.0, 14, cap)
		local clamp = maxLeaf
		for i = 1, #verts do
			local v = verts[i]
			local d, gx, gy, gz = SdfField.fieldGrad(root, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)
			d -= soften
			if d > -clamp and d < clamp then
				verts[i] = Vector3.new(v.X - d * gx, v.Y - d * gy, v.Z - d * gz)
			end
		end
	end

	-- ── Normals (analytic, split at hard edges) + bake ──
	local triCount = #tris / 3
	local faceN = table.create(triCount)
	for fi = 1, triCount do
		local base = (fi - 1) * 3
		local fn = (verts[tris[base + 2]] - verts[tris[base + 1]]):Cross(verts[tris[base + 3]] - verts[tris[base + 1]])
		local m = fn.Magnitude
		faceN[fi] = if m > 1e-9 then fn / m else Vector3.yAxis
	end
	local vN = table.create(#verts)
	for i = 1, #verts do
		local v = verts[i]
		local gx, gy, gz = grad(v.X, v.Y, v.Z)
		vN[i] = Vector3.new(gx, gy, gz)
	end

	local em = AssetService:CreateEditableMesh()
	local vids = table.create(#verts)
	for i, p in ipairs(verts) do
		vids[i] = em:AddVertex(p)
	end
	local fids = table.create(triCount)
	for i = 1, #tris, 3 do
		fids[(i - 1) / 3 + 1] = em:AddTriangle(vids[tris[i]], vids[tris[i + 1]], vids[tris[i + 2]])
	end
	local colorFn = cfg.vertexColorFn
	local cosSharp = math.cos(math.rad(cfg.sharpAngle or 38))
	for fi = 1, triCount do
		local base = (fi - 1) * 3
		local fn = faceN[fi]
		local fid = fids[fi]
		for k = 1, 3 do
			local vi = tris[base + k]
			local an = vN[vi]
			local dp = fn:Dot(an)
			local nrm = if dp >= cosSharp then an else fn
			em:SetVertexFaceNormal(vids[vi], fid, em:AddNormal(nrm))
			if colorFn then
				em:SetVertexFaceColor(vids[vi], fid, em:AddColor(colorFn(verts[vi], nrm, {}, math.clamp(1 - dp, 0, 1)), 1))
			end
		end
	end

	local Content = (getfenv(1) :: any).Content
	local opts: { [string]: any } = {}
	if cfg.renderFidelity then opts.RenderFidelity = cfg.renderFidelity end
	if cfg.collisionFidelity then opts.CollisionFidelity = cfg.collisionFidelity end
	if cfg.fluidFidelity then opts.FluidFidelity = cfg.fluidFidelity end
	local baked
	local okC, errC = pcall(function()
		local res, content
		if next(opts) then
			res, content = AssetService:CreateDataModelContentAsync(Content.fromObject(em), opts)
		else
			res, content = AssetService:CreateDataModelContentAsync(Content.fromObject(em))
		end
		if res ~= Enum.CreateContentResult.Success then
			error("content: " .. tostring(res))
		end
		baked = content
	end)
	em:Destroy()
	if not okC or not baked then
		return nil, "bake content failed: " .. tostring(errC)
	end
	local meshPart
	local okM, errM = pcall(function()
		if next(opts) then
			meshPart = AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(baked, opts)
		else
			meshPart = AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(baked)
		end
	end)
	if not okM or not meshPart then
		return nil, "meshpart failed: " .. tostring(errM)
	end
	if cfg.renderFidelity then pcall(function() (meshPart :: any).RenderFidelity = cfg.renderFidelity end) end
	if cfg.collisionFidelity then pcall(function() (meshPart :: any).CollisionFidelity = cfg.collisionFidelity end) end

	print(string.format(
		"[SdfMesher3] leaves %d | %d→%d tris | octree %.0fms qef %.0fms dc %.0fms decimate %.0fms bake %.0fms total %.0fms",
		leafCount, rawTris, triCount,
		(tSample1 - tSample0) * 1000, (tQef1 - tSample1) * 1000, (tDC1 - tQef1) * 1000,
		(tDecim1 - tDC1) * 1000, (os.clock() - tDecim1) * 1000, (os.clock() - tSample0) * 1000
	))

	return {
		meshPart = meshPart,
		triCount = triCount,
		vertCount = #verts,
		rawTris = rawTris,
		leafCount = leafCount,
		timings = {
			octree = tSample1 - tSample0,
			qef = tQef1 - tSample1,
			dc = tDC1 - tQef1,
			decimate = tDecim1 - tDC1,
			total = os.clock() - tSample0,
		},
	}, string.format("%d tris", triCount)
end

return SdfMesher3

--!strict
-- Generator → kicker handshake. Each ProceduralModel generator should
-- call GeneratorSignal.notify() at the end of OnGenerate; the
-- EditableMeshKicker plugin (and the runtime kicker) use it to throttle
-- the next Version bump so we don't pile up EditableMesh allocations
-- beyond the engine's hard concurrent cap.
--
-- The BindableEvent lives in ReplicatedStorage so the plugin (running
-- outside the generator sandbox) can find the same instance.

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local SIGNAL_NAME = "GeneratorDone"

local GeneratorSignal = {}
GeneratorSignal.SIGNAL_NAME = SIGNAL_NAME

local function ensure(): BindableEvent
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(SIGNAL_NAME)
	if existing and existing:IsA("BindableEvent") then
		return existing
	end
	if existing then
		existing:Destroy()
	end
	local sig = Instance.new("BindableEvent")
	sig.Name = SIGNAL_NAME
	sig.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	return sig
end

-- Diagnostic: counters of every place wrap() can exit, so we can correlate
-- with the kicker's issued/fireCount imbalance reports.
local debugStats = {
	notifyCalls = 0,         -- actual GeneratorSignal.notify() invocations
	bailServer = 0,          -- exited via play-mode-server bail (no notify)
	bailReentrancy = 0,      -- exited via re-entrancy short-circuit (no notify)
	bodyOk = 0,              -- body ran to completion, notify fired
	bodyError = 0,           -- body errored (pcall caught), notify still fired
}
GeneratorSignal._debugStats = debugStats

function GeneratorSignal.notify()
	debugStats.notifyCalls += 1
	pcall(function()
		ensure():Fire()
	end)
end

-- Periodic dump so the kicker can correlate accounting drift with where
-- the missed notifies came from. Once-per-3-seconds rate so it doesn't
-- spam logs.
local lastStatsPrint = 0
local function maybePrintStats()
	local now = os.clock()
	if now - lastStatsPrint < 3 then return end
	lastStatsPrint = now
	print(string.format(
		"[GeneratorSignal] notifies=%d bodyOk=%d bodyErr=%d bailServer=%d bailReentry=%d",
		debugStats.notifyCalls, debugStats.bodyOk, debugStats.bodyError,
		debugStats.bailServer, debugStats.bailReentrancy))
end
GeneratorSignal._maybePrintStats = maybePrintStats

function GeneratorSignal.event(): RBXScriptSignal
	return ensure().Event
end

-- Per-PM re-entrancy guard. ProceduralModel auto-fires OnGenerate any time
-- an attribute changes. Generators that yield (AssetService bake calls are
-- async) can therefore have a SECOND OnGenerate invoked on the same PM
-- mid-bake — both calls then run concurrently in the same generator
-- sandbox, which produces duplicate geometry (the first bake's MeshPart
-- ends up parented alongside the second's) and corrupts any module-level
-- state the generator might use across nested fieldAt-style calls.
--
-- The guard, keyed by the PM's stable Guid attribute (stamped by
-- PolyEdit / similar), short-circuits re-entrant calls and queues a
-- single deferred refire (Version bump) at the end of the in-flight one.
-- That way the latest attribute snapshot still gets baked, but only after
-- the current bake fully completes — no concurrent fires.
--
-- PMs without a Guid attribute (e.g. Tree, Cloud — single-shot bakes that
-- don't yield long enough for re-entry to matter in practice) skip the
-- guard and behave as before.
local inProgressByGuid: { [string]: boolean } = {}
local refireQueuedByGuid: { [string]: boolean } = {}

local function findPMByGuid(guid: string): Instance?
	for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged("HAS_GUID") do
		if inst:GetAttribute("Guid") == guid then return inst end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Wrap a generator's OnGenerate so it always fires the done signal at
-- the end (success, early-return, or error). Errors are pcall'd into a
-- warn so the kicker queue doesn't stall on an exception. Guards against
-- re-entrant calls per PM (see above).
-- One-time warn flag so we don't spam the log if many PMs all try to
-- bake on the play-mode server at the same instant.
local serverBailWarned = false

function GeneratorSignal.wrap(fn: (any, Instance) -> ()): (any, Instance) -> ()
	return function(parameters: any, targetContainer: Instance)
		-- During play, only clients should bake. The server's OnGenerate
		-- would produce duplicate / racing geometry against clients'
		-- bakes (which the engine fires when the PM replicates), and
		-- server-side EditableMesh allocations don't benefit gameplay
		-- since the resulting MeshParts can't replicate cleanly.
		-- Edit-time plugin bakes (IsRunning() == false) still proceed.
		if RunService:IsRunning() and RunService:IsServer() then
			if not serverBailWarned then
				serverBailWarned = true
				warn("[GeneratorSignal] OnGenerate fired on the play-mode SERVER — bailing. (further bails silent for this session)")
			end
			-- Don't fire the done-signal: the kicker uses notify count to
			-- track real bake completions, and the server doesn't bake.
			-- (And the kicker only runs on clients anyway.)
			debugStats.bailServer += 1
			return
		end

		local guid: string? = nil
		local rawGuid = parameters and parameters.Attributes and parameters.Attributes.Guid
		if typeof(rawGuid) == "string" and #rawGuid > 0 then
			guid = rawGuid
		end

		if guid and inProgressByGuid[guid] then
			-- Another OnGenerate for this PM is mid-bake. Queue a refire to
			-- run after it finishes; drop this one to avoid concurrent state.
			-- Don't notify — this OnGenerate didn't actually bake, and
			-- inflating the kicker's fireCount on short-circuits causes it
			-- to think more PMs have completed than actually have, which
			-- pulls inFlight below zero and dispatches more PMs concurrently
			-- than IN_FLIGHT_CAP allows (blowing the EM cap).
			refireQueuedByGuid[guid] = true
			debugStats.bailReentrancy += 1
			-- Diagnostic: re-entry from the engine = something fired
			-- OnGenerate while we were already mid-bake on this PM. The
			-- kicker doesn't know this fire happened, so its issued count
			-- stays correct, but if the IN-FLIGHT call was a kicker
			-- dispatch and this re-entry gets the body to short-circuit,
			-- the *kicker's* OnGenerate gets to notify normally. The
			-- problematic case is the OPPOSITE: kicker dispatches, but
			-- inProgressByGuid is already true (from a prior engine
			-- auto-fire that's still in flight), so the kicker's OnGenerate
			-- gets short-circuited and never notifies. That misses a
			-- fireCount increment.
			print(string.format(
				"[GeneratorSignal] re-entry short-circuit on guid=%s — body skipped, refire queued",
				guid))
			return
		end

		if guid then
			inProgressByGuid[guid] = true
		end

		-- Diagnostic: ProceduralModel does NOT auto-delete previous-bake
		-- children before a new OnGenerate fires. Anything left in the
		-- target container will MERGE with what this fire emits, producing
		-- doubled / stale geometry. If we see leftovers here, either the
		-- previous bake's cleanup didn't run, the kicker / runtime bumped
		-- Version without a stash+detach, or a generator emitted children
		-- it doesn't re-emit on every fire (so there's nothing forcing a
		-- delete). Warn loudly with the names so it's easy to track down.
		local existing = targetContainer:GetChildren()
		if #existing > 0 then
			local names = table.create(#existing)
			for i, c in ipairs(existing) do names[i] = c.Name end
			local guidTag = guid and (" guid=" .. guid) or ""
			warn(string.format("[GeneratorSignal] target container had %d leftover child(ren) at OnGenerate start%s: %s",
				#existing, guidTag, table.concat(names, ", ")))
		end

		local ok, err = pcall(fn, parameters, targetContainer)
		if not ok then
			warn("[GeneratorSignal] generator errored: " .. tostring(err))
			debugStats.bodyError += 1
		else
			debugStats.bodyOk += 1
		end

		if guid then
			inProgressByGuid[guid] = nil
			if refireQueuedByGuid[guid] then
				refireQueuedByGuid[guid] = nil
				-- Defer the refire through the kicker's throttled queue
				-- instead of bumping Version directly. Direct bumps bypass
				-- the IN_FLIGHT_CAP throttle and can blow the EM cap when a
				-- batch of PMs all need refiring at once. The kicker's
				-- rekickAfterByPM flow handles the case where this PM is
				-- still in-flight for the kicker (clearing enqueued and
				-- requeuing happens once the watcher exits).
				--
				-- Lazy-require the kicker so generator sandboxes that don't
				-- have access to it (e.g. running in a context where the
				-- module path doesn't resolve) gracefully fall back to a
				-- direct Version bump.
				local capturedGuid = guid
				task.defer(function()
					local pm = findPMByGuid(capturedGuid)
					if not pm or not pm.Parent then return end
					-- script.Parent.Parent.ProceduralModelKicker resolves to
					-- ReplicatedFirst.ProceduralModelKicker. Lazy-require so
					-- a sandbox without access to it (or a load-order edge
					-- case) falls back to a direct Version bump rather than
					-- erroring out.
					local kickerModule = (script.Parent.Parent :: any):FindFirstChild("ProceduralModelKicker")
					local rOk, kicker = pcall(require, kickerModule)
					if rOk and kicker and (kicker :: any).rekick then
						(kicker :: any).rekick(pm)
					else
						local v = tonumber(pm:GetAttribute("Version")) or 0
						pm:SetAttribute("Version", v + 1)
					end
				end)
			end
		end

		GeneratorSignal.notify()
	end
end

return GeneratorSignal

--!strict
-- FluffyCloud — a self-contained ProceduralModel generator that builds a
-- cumulonimbus cloud out of soft SDF puffs melted together with a generous
-- smooth-blend, shaded with a neutral-intensity + fake-AO + backlit-rim recipe.
--
-- This is the worked example from docs/05-cookbook.md. It depends only on
-- SdfMesher and GeneratorSignal (no WorldSun / palettes / WorldSettings), so it
-- runs as-is in this bundle.
--
-- USAGE: set a ProceduralModel's Generator property to this ModuleScript. The
-- cloud's dimensions follow the PM's Size; its style follows the attributes.

local SdfMesher = require(script.Parent.Parent.Parent.SdfMesher)
local GeneratorSignal = require(script.Parent.Parent.GeneratorSignal)

-- Every field here becomes an editable property in the PM's Studio panel.
-- Changing any of them re-fires OnGenerate.
local Attributes = {
	Seed = 1,
	BaseWidthRatio = 0.48, -- flat-base width / anvil spread
	PuffCount = 95,
	MinPuffRadius = 12,
	MaxPuffRadius = 30,
	SmoothBlend = 6, -- the "fluffiness" knob — high so puffs melt together
	SdfCellsPerDim = 20,
	SdfTriCap = 25000,
	LightColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 250, 240),
	ShadowColor = Color3.fromRGB(70, 80, 100),
	SunDir = Vector3.new(0.4, 0.8, 0.3).Unit,
	Version = 0, -- bump to force a manual re-bake
}

-- XZ width (stud radius) at normalized height yT for a cumulonimbus silhouette:
-- flat base, narrow stem, column, cauliflower bulges, flared anvil cap.
local function widthAt(yT: number, baseWidth: number, anvilSpread: number): number
	if yT < 0.10 then
		return baseWidth * 0.90
	elseif yT < 0.30 then
		return baseWidth * (0.90 - 0.35 * (yT - 0.10) / 0.20)
	elseif yT < 0.70 then
		return baseWidth * 0.55
	elseif yT < 0.90 then
		return baseWidth * 0.55 + (baseWidth * 0.45) * (yT - 0.70) / 0.20
	else
		return baseWidth + (anvilSpread - baseWidth) * (yT - 0.90) / 0.10
	end
end

-- Vertical squash (horizontal mul, vertical mul) per band — squashed base + anvil.
local function squash(yT: number): (number, number)
	if yT < 0.10 then
		return 1.15, 0.55
	elseif yT > 0.90 then
		return 1.30, 0.60
	elseif yT > 0.70 then
		return 1.08, 1.05
	end
	return 1.0, 1.0
end

-- Height sampler biased toward the fluffy upper region.
local function sampleHeightT(rng: Random): number
	local u = rng:NextNumber()
	if u < 0.10 then
		return u / 0.10 * 0.10
	elseif u < 0.50 then
		return 0.10 + (u - 0.10) / 0.40 * 0.60
	elseif u < 0.85 then
		return 0.70 + (u - 0.50) / 0.35 * 0.20
	else
		return 0.90 + (u - 0.85) / 0.15 * 0.10
	end
end

local function OnGenerate(parameters: any, targetContainer: Instance)
	local a = parameters.Attributes
	local size = parameters.Size or Vector3.new(100, 100, 100)
	local height = size.Y
	local maxHoriz = math.min(size.X, size.Z)
	local anvilSpread = maxHoriz
	local baseWidth = anvilSpread * (a.BaseWidthRatio or 0.48)

	local rng = Random.new(a.Seed or 1)
	local minR, maxR = a.MinPuffRadius or 12, a.MaxPuffRadius or 30
	local ellipsoids = {}
	for _ = 1, math.floor(a.PuffCount or 95) do
		local yT = sampleHeightT(rng)
		local w = widthAt(yT, baseWidth, anvilSpread)
		local radialT = math.sqrt(rng:NextNumber()) -- push puffs toward the rim
		local angle = rng:NextNumber() * math.pi * 2
		local r = w * 0.5 * radialT
		local base = minR + rng:NextNumber() * (maxR - minR)
		local hMul, vMul = squash(yT)
		local jitter = 0.85 + rng:NextNumber() * 0.30
		local centeredY = yT * height - height * 0.5 -- base at -h/2, anvil at +h/2
		table.insert(ellipsoids, {
			center = Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * r, centeredY, math.sin(angle) * r),
			semi = Vector3.new(base * hMul * jitter, base * vMul, base * hMul * (2 - jitter)),
		})
	end

	-- Yield slot between cheap planning and the heavy bake so the engine's
	-- watchdog doesn't trip on big puffCount values.
	if parameters.Pause then
		parameters:Pause()
	end

	-- Height/radial reference for the shader.
	local minY, maxY = math.huge, -math.huge
	for _, e in ipairs(ellipsoids) do
		minY = math.min(minY, e.center.Y - e.semi.Y)
		maxY = math.max(maxY, e.center.Y + e.semi.Y)
	end
	local yRange = math.max(maxY - minY, 0.01)
	local horizRef = math.max(maxHoriz * 0.5, 0.01)

	local sunDir = (a.SunDir and a.SunDir.Magnitude > 0.01) and a.SunDir.Unit or Vector3.new(0.4, 0.8, 0.3).Unit
	local lightColor = a.LightColor or Color3.fromRGB(255, 250, 240)
	local shadowColor = a.ShadowColor or Color3.fromRGB(70, 80, 100)

	-- Neutral-intensity shader: accumulate all light into a single scalar, then
	-- lerp shadow→light by it. Fake AO darkens creases; fake SSS rim glows on
	-- the anti-sun silhouette edges.
	local function colorFn(vertex: Vector3, normal: Vector3): Color3
		local heightT = math.clamp((vertex.Y - minY) / yRange, 0, 1)
		local radialT = math.clamp(math.sqrt(vertex.X * vertex.X + vertex.Z * vertex.Z) / horizRef, 0, 1)
		local key = math.max(0, normal:Dot(sunDir))
		local sky = math.max(0, normal.Y * 0.5 + 0.5)
		local grn = math.max(0, -normal.Y)
		local intensity = key * 0.55 + sky * 0.35 + grn * 0.18 + 0.12
		intensity *= (1 - math.max(0, -normal.Y) * heightT * heightT * 0.40) -- fake AO
		local antiKey = math.max(0, -normal:Dot(sunDir))
		local edgeness = 1 - math.abs(normal.Y)
		intensity += (antiKey ^ 1.2) * (edgeness ^ 1.5) * (0.5 + radialT * 0.5) * 0.85 -- SSS rim
		return shadowColor:Lerp(lightColor, math.clamp(intensity, 0, 1))
	end

	local result, msg = SdfMesher.build({ ellipsoids = ellipsoids }, {
		triCap = math.floor(a.SdfTriCap or 25000),
		initialMaxCellsPerDim = math.floor(a.SdfCellsPerDim or 20),
		boundsPadding = 4,
		smoothBlend = a.SmoothBlend or 6,
		vertexColorFn = colorFn,
		renderFidelity = Enum.RenderFidelity.Precise,
		collisionFidelity = Enum.CollisionFidelity.Box,
	})
	if not result then
		warn("[FluffyCloud] bake failed: " .. tostring(msg))
		return
	end

	local mp = result.meshPart
	mp.Name = "Cloud"
	mp.Anchored = true
	mp.CanCollide = false
	mp.CastShadow = false
	mp.CanQuery = false
	mp.CanTouch = false
	mp.AudioCanCollide = false
	-- Neon blows out at pure white — knock the part color down so highlights
	-- have headroom and don't clip to solid white.
	mp.Color = Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200)
	mp.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	mp.Size = size
	mp.Parent = targetContainer
end

return {
	Attributes = Attributes,
	OnGenerate = GeneratorSignal.wrap(OnGenerate),
}

--!strict
-- Shared helpers for the garden/park ProceduralModel generators.
-- Kept deliberately small — just snow-sprinkle helpers and mesh mount.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local SdfMesher = require(script.Parent.Parent.Parent.SdfMesher)

local GeneratorUtil = {}

-- Global snow coverage scalar. Lives at
-- ReplicatedStorage.WorldSettings.SnowAmount as a 0..1 number (0 = no
-- snow, 1 = full coverage). Replaces the per-PM GenerateWithSnow boolean
-- so seasonal/climate changes can flip the world from one place. Returns
-- 1 if WorldSettings is missing, so old scenes keep working.
function GeneratorUtil.getSnowAmount(): number
	local ws = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("WorldSettings")
	if not ws then return 1 end
	local v = ws:GetAttribute("SnowAmount")
	if typeof(v) == "number" then
		return math.clamp(v, 0, 1)
	end
	return 1
end

-- Global leaf coverage scalar at WorldSettings.LeafAmount (0..1, default 1).
-- Linear shrink: 0 = bare trees, 1 = full canopy. Generators that consume
-- this typically multiply their foliage radii by it. Returns 1 if missing
-- so old scenes keep their default leafy look.
function GeneratorUtil.getLeafAmount(): number
	local ws = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("WorldSettings")
	if not ws then return 1 end
	local v = ws:GetAttribute("LeafAmount")
	if typeof(v) == "number" then
		return math.clamp(v, 0, 1)
	end
	return 1
end

-- Probabilistic thinning: each blob is kept with probability `amount`.
-- Used to scale snow coverage with WorldSettings.SnowAmount. Seeded by
-- the generator's own seed so the same PM thins to the same blobs each
-- bake (no flicker on regen). 0 returns empty, 1 returns input unchanged.
function GeneratorUtil.thinSnow(snowEllipsoids: { any }, amount: number, seed: number?): { any }
	if amount >= 1 then return snowEllipsoids end
	if amount <= 0 then return {} end
	local rng = Random.new(seed or 1)
	local out = {}
	for _, e in ipairs(snowEllipsoids) do
		if rng:NextNumber() < amount then
			table.insert(out, e)
		end
	end
	return out
end

-- Resolve a generator color attribute. The PM's color "attributes" are
-- now strings naming an entry on ReplicatedStorage.Palettes.<generatorName>
-- (a Configuration whose attributes are Color3s). Lets us recolor every
-- placed instance from a single Configuration. Falls back to the in-code
-- default if the palette / attribute is missing, or if the value passed
-- in is already a Color3 (legacy data on placed PMs that pre-dates the
-- string switch — they keep working until someone wipes the override).
function GeneratorUtil.resolveColor(generatorName: string, value: any, fallback: Color3): Color3
	if typeof(value) == "Color3" then
		return value
	end
	if typeof(value) ~= "string" or #value == 0 then
		return fallback
	end
	local palettes = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Palettes")
	if not palettes then return fallback end
	local config = palettes:FindFirstChild(generatorName)
	if not config then return fallback end
	local resolved = config:GetAttribute(value)
	if typeof(resolved) == "Color3" then
		return resolved
	end
	return fallback
end

-- Flattened snow domes on top of each source ellipsoid. Returns a new
-- ellipsoid list ready to append to the bake input.
function GeneratorUtil.snowOnEllipsoids(
	ellipsoids: { any },
	opts: { radiusMul: number?, flatness: number?, offsetMul: number? }?
): { any }
	opts = opts or {}
	local rMul = opts.radiusMul or 0.72
	local flat = opts.flatness or 0.40
	local offMul = opts.offsetMul or 0.55
	local out = {}
	for _, e in ipairs(ellipsoids) do
		local r = (e.semi.X + e.semi.Z) * 0.5 * rMul
		table.insert(out, {
			center = e.center + Vector3.new(0, e.semi.Y * offMul, 0),
			semi = Vector3.new(r, r * flat, r),
		})
	end
	return out
end

-- Snow beads riding the upward-facing side of each non-vertical capsule.
function GeneratorUtil.snowOnCapsules(
	capsules: { any },
	opts: { radiusMul: number?, flatness: number?, verticalityFloor: number? }?
): { any }
	opts = opts or {}
	local rMul = opts.radiusMul or 0.5
	local flat = opts.flatness or 0.40
	local floor = opts.verticalityFloor or 0.20
	local out = {}
	for _, cap in ipairs(capsules) do
		local diff = cap.b - cap.a
		local len = diff.Magnitude
		if len < 0.1 then continue end
		local dir = diff / len
		local tan = Vector3.new(-dir.X * dir.Y, 1 - dir.Y * dir.Y, -dir.Z * dir.Y)
		local tanMag = tan.Magnitude
		if tanMag < floor then continue end
		tan = tan / tanMag
		local r = cap.radius * rMul
		local ry = r * flat
		local offset = cap.radius * 0.75
		local spacing = math.max(r * 0.7, 0.3)
		local n = math.max(1, math.floor(len / spacing))
		for i = 0, n do
			local t = i / n
			local c = cap.a + diff * t + tan * offset
			table.insert(out, {
				center = c,
				semi = Vector3.new(r, ry, r),
			})
		end
	end
	return out
end

-- Coat the upward-facing parts of a built SDF surface with snow blobs
-- by sphere-tracing downward at a regular grid spacing in XZ. Each ray
-- that hits the surface drops a flattened ellipsoid (oval sphere) at
-- the hit point, oriented so its bottom kisses the surface. Steep /
-- vertical / underside surfaces fail the normal-Y threshold and stay
-- bare, so the result follows the actual sloped silhouette of carved
-- shapes (rocks, fences, terrain) instead of just sitting on top of
-- the source primitives like the legacy snowOnEllipsoids does.
--
-- `input` is the same table you'd hand to SdfMesher.build — same
-- ellipsoids/slabs/capsules/subtracts. The snow blobs returned can be
-- fed straight to bakeSnow.
function GeneratorUtil.snowOnSurface(
	input: any,
	opts: {
		ballRadius: number?, -- horizontal half-extent of each snow oval
		flatness: number?, -- vertical / horizontal radius ratio (< 1 = squashed)
		gridSpacing: number?, -- XZ grid step. Smaller = denser coverage
		jitter: number?, -- per-sample random XZ jitter as a fraction of gridSpacing
		minNormalY: number?, -- reject surfaces whose normal.Y is below this
		maxRayDist: number?, -- cap on sphere-trace length
		startMargin: number?, -- studs above the bounds top to start each ray
		-- Fraction (0..1) of footprint samples that must hit the surface
		-- within ±ballRadius of the center hit's Y for the blob to count
		-- as resting on rock. Higher = stricter, kills blobs that hang
		-- over edges. 1.0 = fully supported only; 0.6–0.8 = some
		-- tolerance for natural corners.
		supportThreshold: number?,
		-- Number of XZ directions sampled at radius ballR around each
		-- center hit when checking footprint support.
		supportSamples: number?,
		seed: number?,
	}?
): { any }
	opts = opts or {}
	local ballRadius = opts.ballRadius or 0.6
	local flatness = opts.flatness or 0.35
	local gridSpacing = opts.gridSpacing or (ballRadius * 0.9)
	local jitter = math.clamp(opts.jitter or 0.4, 0, 0.5)
	local minNormalY = opts.minNormalY or 0.45
	local maxRayDist = opts.maxRayDist or 200
	local startMargin = opts.startMargin or 1
	local supportThreshold = math.clamp(opts.supportThreshold or 0.75, 0, 1)
	local supportSamples = math.max(4, math.floor(opts.supportSamples or 8))
	local seed = opts.seed or 1

	local minV, maxV = SdfMesher.computeInputBounds(input)
	if not minV or not maxV then return {} end

	local sdfFn = SdfMesher.makeSdfFn(input)

	-- Sphere-trace downward from above the bounds. The SDF gives a
	-- conservative step distance at every iteration, so we never
	-- overshoot a feature smaller than the current SDF value. ~80
	-- iterations is plenty for any reasonable rock-sized shape.
	local function traceDown(x: number, z: number): Vector3?
		local startY = maxV.Y + startMargin
		local t = 0
		for _ = 1, 80 do
			if t >= maxRayDist then return nil end
			local y = startY - t
			if y < minV.Y - ballRadius then return nil end
			local p = Vector3.new(x, y, z)
			local d = sdfFn(p)
			if d < 0.01 then return p end
			t += d
		end
		return nil
	end

	-- SDF gradient via central differences. The gradient points OUTWARD
	-- of the surface (away from the interior), so it's already the
	-- outward normal direction once normalized. Step size of half a ball
	-- radius is plenty fine without amplifying numeric noise.
	local h = math.max(0.05, ballRadius * 0.5)
	local function normalAt(p: Vector3): Vector3
		local dx = sdfFn(p + Vector3.new(h, 0, 0)) - sdfFn(p - Vector3.new(h, 0, 0))
		local dy = sdfFn(p + Vector3.new(0, h, 0)) - sdfFn(p - Vector3.new(0, h, 0))
		local dz = sdfFn(p + Vector3.new(0, 0, h)) - sdfFn(p - Vector3.new(0, 0, h))
		local g = Vector3.new(dx, dy, dz)
		local mag = g.Magnitude
		if mag < 1e-6 then return Vector3.new(0, 1, 0) end
		return g / mag
	end

	-- Footprint support: trace a ring of `supportSamples` rays straight
	-- down from above, at radius ballRadius around the center hit. Count
	-- how many find rock close enough (within ±ballRadius vertically) to
	-- be supporting the blob. Catches placements where the center is on
	-- rock but the ball hangs out into air past an edge — the cardinal-
	-- direction samples there will either miss the rock entirely or hit
	-- way down on a cliff face, both failing the proximity test.
	local supportNeeded = math.ceil(supportSamples * supportThreshold)
	local supportYTolerance = ballRadius
	local function isFootprintSupported(hit: Vector3): boolean
		if supportNeeded <= 0 then return true end
		local supported = 0
		local missLimit = supportSamples - supportNeeded -- early-out when survival is impossible
		local missed = 0
		for k = 1, supportSamples do
			local theta = (k / supportSamples) * math.pi * 2
			local sx = hit.X + math.cos(theta) * ballRadius
			local sz = hit.Z + math.sin(theta) * ballRadius
			local edgeHit = traceDown(sx, sz)
			if edgeHit and math.abs(edgeHit.Y - hit.Y) <= supportYTolerance then
				supported += 1
				if supported >= supportNeeded then return true end
			else
				missed += 1
				if missed > missLimit then return false end
			end
		end
		return supported >= supportNeeded
	end

	local rng = Random.new(seed)
	local out = {}
	local ballHalfY = ballRadius * flatness
	-- Lift each ball so most of it sits ABOVE the surface — bottom
	-- ~20% intersects the host so the SDF blends visually but the
	-- silhouette reads as a snow cap, not a half-buried disk.
	local centerLift = ballHalfY * 0.6

	local x = minV.X
	while x <= maxV.X do
		local z = minV.Z
		while z <= maxV.Z do
			local jx = (rng:NextNumber() - 0.5) * 2 * jitter * gridSpacing
			local jz = (rng:NextNumber() - 0.5) * 2 * jitter * gridSpacing
			local hit = traceDown(x + jx, z + jz)
			if hit then
				local n = normalAt(hit)
				if n.Y >= minNormalY and isFootprintSupported(hit) then
					table.insert(out, {
						center = hit + Vector3.new(0, centerLift, 0),
						semi = Vector3.new(ballRadius, ballHalfY, ballRadius),
					})
				end
			end
			z += gridSpacing
		end
		x += gridSpacing
	end

	return out
end

-- Standard mount: applied to every MeshPart the generators produce.
function GeneratorUtil.mountMesh(
	mp: MeshPart,
	container: Instance,
	props: { [string]: any }?
)
	mp.Anchored = true
	mp.CanCollide = false
	mp.CastShadow = true
	mp.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	if props then
		for k, v in pairs(props) do
			(mp :: any)[k] = v
		end
	end
	mp.Parent = container
end

-- Bake a separate Snow MeshPart from the given ellipsoids and parent it.
-- Keeping snow on its own mesh lets it carry Enum.Material.Snow + a
-- neutral white color independently of the host prop's material. Skips
-- cleanly when the ellipsoid list is empty.
local FALLBACK_SNOW_TOP = Color3.fromRGB(245, 248, 253)
local FALLBACK_SNOW_UNDER = Color3.fromRGB(170, 195, 225)

function GeneratorUtil.bakeSnow(
	snowEllipsoids: { any },
	targetContainer: Instance,
	opts: { triCap: number?, cellsPerDim: number?, smoothBlend: number?, color: Color3? }?
)
	if #snowEllipsoids == 0 then return end
	opts = opts or {}
	-- Two-tone snow shading: bright white on up-facing surfaces (sunlit
	-- caps), cool blue on down-facing / underside surfaces (sky bounce
	-- + shadow). normal.Y maps from -1 (full under) to +1 (full top); we
	-- remap to 0..1 with a gentle bias so the upper hemisphere reads as
	-- mostly white and the under-tint kicks in on the truly downward bits.
	local topColor = GeneratorUtil.resolveColor("Snow", "Top", FALLBACK_SNOW_TOP)
	local underColor = GeneratorUtil.resolveColor("Snow", "Under", FALLBACK_SNOW_UNDER)
	local function snowColorFn(_vertex: Vector3, normal: Vector3, _w: { [string]: number }): Color3
		local t = math.clamp(normal.Y * 0.5 + 0.5, 0, 1)
		-- Sharpen: most of the mesh stays top-color, only the bottom
		-- ~third pushes hard into under-color. A linear lerp washed out
		-- the silhouette into uniform pale blue.
		t = math.clamp((t - 0.35) / 0.4, 0, 1)
		return underColor:Lerp(topColor, t)
	end
	local result, msg = SdfMesher.build(
		{ ellipsoids = snowEllipsoids },
		{
			-- Bumped from 4000 → 6000: at smoothBlend=0.9 (RockCrystal's
			-- "continuous tube" snow look) tri counts routinely landed at
			-- ~4500, forcing a triangle-cap retry that doubled the bake
			-- time. 6000 leaves headroom without producing visibly heavier
			-- meshes.
			triCap = opts.triCap or 6000,
			initialMaxCellsPerDim = opts.cellsPerDim or 40,
			boundsPadding = 2,
			smoothBlend = opts.smoothBlend or 0.45,
			vertexColorFn = snowColorFn,
			renderFidelity = Enum.RenderFidelity.Precise,
			collisionFidelity = Enum.CollisionFidelity.Box,
		}
	)
	if not result then
		warn("[GeneratorUtil.bakeSnow] bake failed: " .. tostring(msg))
		return
	end
	-- MeshPart.Color stays white so the per-vertex colors carry the look;
	-- if `opts.color` is passed, multiply on top via Color (rare path).
	GeneratorUtil.mountMesh(result.meshPart, targetContainer, {
		Name = "Snow",
		Color = opts.color or Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
		Material = Enum.Material.Snow,
	})
end

return GeneratorUtil
